recommendations.text: Primary survey with TBSA estimation and airway assessment is the critical first step in burn management.

For Burn Initial Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess airway (within 5 minutes) - assess vital signs (within 5 minutes) - estimate tbsa (within 15 minutes) - assess burn depth - obtain patient weight - establish iv access (within 15 minutes)
During Burn Initial Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: apply ice to burn, apply butter to burn, debride in field.
Parkland formula (4ml x kg x %TBSA) with LR in first 24h. Titrate to urine output 0.5ml/kg/h.

For Fluid Resuscitation, the following actions are mandatory: - calculate parkland formula (within 30 minutes) - start lactated ringers (within 30 minutes) - monitor urine output target 0 5 ml kg h - titrate fluids to urine output - place foley catheter (within 60 minutes)
During Fluid Resuscitation, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give colloid in first 24h, use normal saline only.

Children <5 have limited glycogen stores. Large fluid resuscitation without dextrose causes hypoglycemia. Add D5 to maintenance fluids.
 [REQUIRED: add_dextrose_to_iv, monitor_glucose_q4h] (Severity: HIGH)

Pediatric burn patients deplete glycogen rapidly; dextrose-free resuscitation without glucose monitoring causes hypoglycemic seizures. [FORBIDDEN: withhold_glucose_monitoring_pediatric_burn, give_dextrose_free_fluid_only_pediatric_burn] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ABA Burn Guidelines 2023; pediatric patients have limited glycogen reserves; hypoglycemia causes seizures and brain injury

recommendations.text:
>40% TBSA burns risk fluid creep (>6ml/kg/%TBSA). Excessive resuscitation causes abdominal compartment syndrome, pulmonary edema. Cap at ~6ml/kg/%TBSA and consider colloid adjunct early.
 [FORBIDDEN: exceed_6ml_kg_tbsa_in_24h] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: ABA 2024; Saffle JR, J Burn Care Res 2007 - fluid creep

recommendations.text: Early intubation is critical as airway edema progresses rapidly. 100% O2 for CO poisoning.

For Inhalation Injury Management, the following actions are mandatory: - perform early intubation (within 15 minutes) - order chest xray - order carboxyhemoglobin (within 30 minutes) - give 100 percent oxygen (within 5 minutes)
During Inhalation Injury Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay intubation for imaging.

Enclosed space fire -> cyanide poisoning from combustion of synthetic materials. Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit) is first-line. Do NOT use sodium thiosulfate as sole treatment (too slow onset).
 [REQUIRED: give_hydroxocobalamin, order_cyanide_level] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Sodium nitrite creates methemoglobin which compounds CO poisoning in burns; cyanide level delays allow fatal exposure. [FORBIDDEN: give_sodium_nitrite_in_cyanide_burn, delay_cyanide_antidote_for_level] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ABA Burn Guidelines 2023; sodium nitrite induces methemoglobinemia compounding carbon monoxide poisoning in burn patients

recommendations.text: Circumferential full-thickness burns require escharotomy to prevent vascular compromise and ventilatory failure.
For Escharotomy, the following actions are mandatory: - assess compartment pressures - assess distal pulses (within 30 minutes) - perform escharotomy (within 60 minutes)

Circumferential chest burns restrict chest wall compliance -> ventilatory failure. Chest escharotomy restores compliance. Monitor peak airway pressures.
 [REQUIRED: perform_chest_escharotomy, monitor_ventilation_pressures] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Chest eschar restricts ventilation; delaying escharotomy for imaging or increasing ventilator pressure without release is harmful. [FORBIDDEN: delay_escharotomy_for_imaging, increase_ventilator_pressure_without_escharotomy] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ABA Burn Guidelines 2023; circumferential chest eschar causes restrictive ventilatory failure requiring emergent release

recommendations.text: Initial wound care focuses on clean dry dressings. Defer topical antibiotics to burn center preference.

For Burn Wound Care, the following actions are mandatory: - remove clothing jewelry (within 30 minutes) - cover with clean dry dressing - update tetanus if needed - pain management (within 30 minutes)
During Burn Wound Care, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: apply topical antibiotic before transfer.
Burns >20% TBSA, full-thickness >5%, inhalation injury, and extremes of age require burn center referral.
For Transfer Disposition, the following actions are mandatory: - assess burn center referral criteria (within 120 minutes) - arrange transfer if indicated
During Transfer Disposition, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge major burn home.
